content.title: About
content.content: General Tso chicken is a popular Chinese‑American dish featuring bite‑size pieces of chicken breast coated in a light batter, deep‑fried, and tossed in a sweet‑spicy sauce made from soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, garlic, and ginger. It is commonly served with rice or noodles.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish is named after Zuo Zongtang, a Qing‑ dynasty general, although there is no historical connection.
It originated in California restaurants in the 1970s, not in China.
Many sauce variations exist; some recipes add sesame oil, others use chili sauce for extra heat.
General Tso chicken is considered an “American” Chinese dish and is a staple of fast‑casual Chinese food.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Chicken breast provides a complete source of protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains vitamins B6 and B12, which support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Chicken supplies iron, zinc, and phosphorus, important for blood health and bones.

items.title: High sugar and sodium
items.content: The sauce often contains a lot of sugar and soy sauce, which can raise blood sugar and blood pressure.

items.title: Spicy ingredients
items.content: People with sensitive stomachs or gastritis should limit intake because of the sauce’s heat.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: If you are allergic to soy, use a soy‑free alternative sauce.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve General Tso chicken hot, garnished with toasted sesame seeds and sliced green onions. It pairs well with steamed rice, fried noodles, or a vegetable side.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. When frozen, it keeps its flavor for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly before serving.
